papers.title: Synthesis and Characterization of the Proposed 1,4-Dihydropyridinate Intermediate with a Nickel-Pincer Nucleotide Cofactor Model Complex
papers.titleOriginal:
Synthesis and Characterization
of the Proposed 1,4-Dihydropyridinate
Intermediate with a Nickel-Pincer Nucleotide Cofactor Model Complex
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract The nickel pincer nucleotide (NPN) cofactor was structurally characterized in lactate racemase in 2014, and it is now known that NPN is important in a superfamily of enzymes responsible for isomerization of α-hydroxyacids and also important in other hydride transfer reactions across bacteria and archaea. A decade of biochemical and theoretical studies have led to proposals for the mechanism of reaction for the NPN, but structural or spectroscopic characterization of a well-defined intermediate in the mechanisms has been elusive. Herein, we report a synthetic model of the NPN cofactor which is faithful to the cofactor in consisting of a di(thioamide) substituted pyridine ring. The hydride transfer reactivity of the NPN model was studied and both 1,4- and 1,2-dihydropyridinates (DHP–) of both the free ligand and the Ni complex have been isolated and studied spectroscopically. No evidence for Ni-hydride formation was observed. The UV–vis spectrum of the 1,4-DHP– Ni model complex (1H1,4) has features matching UV–vis spectra collected in biochemical studies where NaBH4 was added to the NPN-dependent enzyme, lactate racemase; whereas the spectra of 1-I and 1H1,2 do not match spectra collected from NPN cofactor reaction intermediates. Thus, the isolation and characterization of 1H1,4 reported herein provides the first direct experimental evidence assigning the reactivity observed in biochemical studies to the pyridyl C4 position of a NPN cofactor model complex.

papers.title: The chemical evolution of the Large Magellanic Cloud from APOGEE abundances: A hybrid two-infall OMEGA+ analysis
papers.titleOriginal: The chemical evolution of the Large Magellanic Cloud from APOGEE abundances: A hybrid two-infall OMEGA+ analysis
papers.journal: Astronomy & Astrophysics
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: The Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) provides resolved stellar abundances and star formation histories (SFHs) that can be used together to test models of dwarf-galaxy chemical evolution. We investigated if the non-monotonic APOGEE $ Mg / Fe -- Fe / H $ sequence can be explained by a hybrid history that combines a second gas-infall episode with a temporary increase in star formation efficiency (SFE). We selected 4933 LMC red giant branch stars from APOGEE-2 DR17. We fitted an adaptively binned median Mg sequence with the two-zone open-box code . The formal fitting objective contained only the Mg sequence. The metallicity distribution function (MDF), one-dimensional abundance distributions, SFH, present-day mass partition, star formation rate (SFR), and supernova (SN) rate were retained as posterior diagnostics. OMEGA+ The best-fitting model reproduces the Mg sequence with a root mean square (RMS) residual of 0.01 dex and also gives a close posterior match to O. It contains two delayed-tau infall episodes, with the second beginning at t_2=10.39 Gyr and with an integrated mass ratio of M_2/M_1=0.159, followed by a temporary Gaussian SFE enhancement centered at t=11.91 Gyr. The second infall is represented by a mixture of enriched and primordial gas. The model reproduces the timing of the late SFH enhancement and yields a present SFR within the adopted comparison range. A hybrid second-infall and SFE enhancement history is a plausible scenario for reproducing the observed LMC Mg median sequence. Our fit explains the LMC evolution fairly well, but the remaining small MDF, mass, and SN rate discrepancies suggest that a selection-function-aware treatment of the stellar distributions is required for a stricter comparison.

papers.title: Synthesis and Crystal Structure of Bulk Methanetetrol C(OH)4
papers.titleOriginal:
Synthesis and Crystal
Structure of Bulk Methanetetrol
C(OH)4
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Methanetetrol, C(OH)4 (orthocarbonic acid), is an elusive tethrahydroxymethane that, due to its rapid dissociation under ambient conditions, has never been synthesized in bulk. A recent study detected the formation of C(OH)4 molecules in the gas phase. Here, we show that C(OH)4 can be synthesized in a diamond anvil cell through the reaction between H2O and CO2 at 45(3) GPa and 50(3) GPa and temperatures <1200(200) K. The crystal structure of C(OH)4 was determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and corroborated by density-functional theory calculations together with Raman spectroscopy. It is composed of isolated [C(OH)4]-molecules linked by strong hydrogen bonds. Under high-pressure conditions, orthocarbonic and carbonic acids are denser than coexisting water ice phases, allowing them to segregate gravitationally and form stable reservoirs of oxidized carbon. These phases incorporate large amounts of carbon into their crystal structures as part of [CO4]4–- or [CO3]2–-building blocks. Because the amount of carbon that can be stored as CO2 in clathrates or filled-ices is significantly smaller, orthocarbonic and carbonic acids may provide a host mechanism for sequestering large carbon inventories in the icy mantles of water-rich exoplanets.

papers.titleOriginal: Neutron star-companion interaction in core-collapse supernovae. Population synthesis based on detailed binary evolution models
papers.journal: Astronomy & Astrophysics
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Most massive stars live in binary systems. When the first supernova in a binary occurs, the ejecta hit the companion, which may inflate as a consequence, and then interact with the newly formed compact object. The recent Type Ic supernova shows a periodic modulation in its emission, which is interpreted as evidence of such interaction. 2022jli We derive predictions for the occurrence rate and observables of supernovae exhibiting these compact object--companion interactions (CCIs). We analyzed a comprehensive state-of-the-art grid of detailed binary stellar evolution models and implemented analytic prescriptions for the expansion of the companion star following its interaction with the supernova ejecta. We then employed the newly developed population synthesis code to derive the distribution functions of the properties of the supernovae affected by CCI and their companions, where we used different explodability and neutron star birth-kick distributions. SN-ORACLE We find that periodic CCI is expected to occur in more than half of the binary systems that produce a hydrogen-poor core-collapse supernova and are not disrupted, while the occurrence rate in systems producing hydrogen-rich supernovae is small. We found broad period ranges, peaking around 20-50 with the interaction lasting for 0.5-10 , , and . The inflation of the companion also increases their luminosity and brightness, increasing their detectability with current instruments. For , our best-fitting models predict a J-band magnitude of 21-23 for up to sim10 We identified specific binary evolution models that reproduce the observed period of the light curve undulations of 2022jli 2015ap 2022esa 2022jli We find that up to sim27% of H-poor supernovae could show periodicity in their light curves, while only a few such events have been identified so far. Our results may help identify periodic CCI features in future and archival supernova observations.

papers.abstract: We report the first measurement of the semileptonic decay $D^+_s \rightarrow K^*(892)^0μ^+ν_μ$ and an improved measurement of the decay $D^+_s \rightarrow K^*(892)^0 e^+ν_{e}$ using a sample of $7.33~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of $e^+e^-$ annihilation data collected at center-of-mass energies between 4.128 to 4.226~GeV with the BESIII detector at the BEPCII collider. We measure the branching fractions to be $\mathcal B({D^+_s\rightarrow K^*(892)^0 μ^+ν_μ})=(2.07\pm0.22_{\rm stat}\pm0.10_{\rm syst})\times10^{-3}$ and $\mathcal B({D^+_s\rightarrow K^*(892)^0 e^+ν_{e}})=(2.14\pm0.18_{\rm stat}\pm0.10_{\rm syst})\times10^{-3}$. Based on a simultaneous study of the dynamics in two semileptonic decays, the hadronic form factor parameters in the $D^+_s\rightarrow K^{*}(892)^0$ transition are determined to be $r_{V} = V(0)/A_1(0) = 1.63 \pm 0.14_{\rm stat} \pm 0.08_{\rm syst}$, $r_{2} = A_2(0)/A_1(0) = 0.60 \pm 0.13_{\rm stat} \pm 0.06_{\rm syst}$, and $A_1(0)=0.56 \pm 0.02_{\rm stat} \pm 0.01_{\rm syst}$, where $V(0)$ is the vector form factor and $A_{1,2}(0)$ are the axial-vector form factors evaluated at $q^2=0$. The precision of $r_V$ and $r_2$ is improved by twofold and $A_1(0)$ is measured for the first time. We also report the first model-independent measurements of the differential decay rates and the lepton forward-backward asymmetries for $D^+_s\rightarrow K^{*}(892)^0\ell^+ν_{\ell}$ decays. Based on these measurements, we perform a test of lepton flavor universality in full and separate $q^2$ intervals with $D^+_s\rightarrow K^{*}(892)^0\ell^+ν_{\ell}$ decays. No violation is found within uncertainties. Our results present for the first time a complete study of the dynamics in the $D_s^+\rightarrow K^*(892)^0$ transition, and provide stringent tests of various non-perturbative theoretical calculations.

papers.title: Galaxy clusters in the VIDEO fields: Detection and characterisation in the context of MOONRISE
papers.titleOriginal: Galaxy clusters in the VIDEO fields: Detection and characterisation in the context of MOONRISE
papers.journal: Astronomy & Astrophysics
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: The identification and characterisation of galaxy clusters at different cosmic times are fundamental to constrain cosmological scenarios and to understand the joint evolution of structure formation and galaxies in dense environments. In this work, we analyse the cluster content of the ∼ 4.5 ^ deg 2 XMM-LSS and CDFS VIDEO fields, which are expected to be partially covered by the upcoming MOONRISE survey. Using AMICO and WaZP photometric redshift-based cluster finders, we constructed a sample of 519 cluster candidates detected by both finders in the redshift range z = 0.1-3, including 74 detections at z > 1.5. For all detections, we identifed the brightest central galaxy (BCG) and computed a list of probabilistic cluster memberships. Our photometric redshift measurements of the clusters agree well with spectroscopic redshifts from the literature, when available. From ancillary spectroscopic data, we assign z_ measurements to 116 cluster candidates based on their spectroscopic members and to 204 based on their likely BCGs. We also show that candidates containing radio-loud members were efficiently recovered using the prior-based cluster finder PPM. We perform a preliminary analysis of the galaxy content of these candidates, focusing on the red-sequence components of their apparent colour-magnitude diagram. By comparing their mean colours with models of galaxy evolution, we show that this population is consistent with a model of passive evolution with a formation at high redshift, and is already in place at z = 1.5-2.0. Finally, our cluster sample was used to evaluate how these clusters would be detected and characterised, according to various MOONRISE strategies. We show that cluster spectroscopic confirmation and characterisation could be efficiently achieved up to z even with the shallowest survey strategy. This brings unprecedented insight into the physical properties of high-redshift galaxy clusters and into galaxy formation in dense environments.

papers.title: Dynamics of Polypropylene Chains at a Model Catalytic Interface Revealed by Quasielastic Neutron Scattering: Can Interfacial Diffusivity Predict Reactivity in Chemical Recycling?
papers.titleOriginal:
Dynamics of Polypropylene
Chains at a Model Catalytic
Interface Revealed by Quasielastic Neutron Scattering: Can Interfacial
Diffusivity Predict Reactivity in Chemical Recycling?
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Catalytic processes developed for petroleum refining, such as bifunctional hydrocracking, can be adopted to chemically recycle plastic polymers. In these reactions, polymer substrates often exhibit distinct kinetics from small molecules with identical chemical structures, emphasizing that the macromolecular behavior of polymer chains beyond local bonding modulates the reactivity. Here, we report the direct measurement of the dynamics of polymer chains at a model catalytic interface, using quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS). Three polypropylenes (PPs) of varying chain lengths and tacticities were studied. In all cases, polymer–catalyst interaction leads to the loss of bulk melting behavior, and segmental dynamics of PP chains can be described by continuous translational diffusion. A lower activation barrier and less favored entropy change at the transition state were observed at the catalytic interface relative to bulk melts, leading to reduced segmental diffusivity at reaction temperatures. The interfacial dynamics are faster for isotactic PP than for atactic PP. This difference is absent in the melt and rationalizes the higher reactivity of isotactic PP in diffusion-limited hydrocracking. This work pioneers the use of H-sensitive neutron-based techniques to probe the consequential macromolecular behaviors of reacting polymer chains at catalytic interfaces. The integration of such novel fundamental knowledge into bonding-level chemical kinetics can transform the understanding of catalytic polymer recycling reactions into a holistic framework, enabling the accurate explanation and prediction of phenomena not accounted for by traditional kinetic approaches.

papers.title: Polar-structure galaxies beyond the local Universe: First results from Euclid
papers.titleOriginal: Polar-structure galaxies beyond the local Universe: First results from Euclid
papers.journal: Astronomy & Astrophysics
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Galaxies hosting strongly misaligned stellar and gas structures offer a direct window into external accretion and the buildup of angular momentum through multiple spin components. Such polar-structure systems are intrinsically rare and have been identified almost entirely at low redshift so far. The Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1) with its uniform space-based Visible Instrument imaging provides an unprecedented opportunity to locate these objects over wide areas and at much greater distances. We present the first visual search for polar-structure galaxy (PSG) candidates in Euclid Visible Instrument data, spanning approximately 10% of the Q1 survey footprint. This search yields the largest high-redshift PSG candidate sample assembled to date, including roughly 100 high-confidence systems with over 50 at z ≳ 0.3, along with additional populations of face-on rings and polar tidal structures. Robust candidates are detected out to redshifts of z demonstrating that polar structures can be identified well beyond the local Universe. Although the present sample is not yet sufficient for quantitative occurrence rate or evolutionary measurements, it enables initial classification and basic structural characterization of PSGs at intermediate redshift. These results lay the groundwork for future statistical studies with forthcoming Euclid data releases and illustrate Euclid’s power for rare-object science across cosmic time.

papers.title: Unraveling the Intrinsic Interfacial Chemistry of Fluoroethylene Carbonate on Lithium Metal Anodes via a Solvent-Free Model System
papers.titleOriginal:
Unraveling the Intrinsic
Interfacial Chemistry of
Fluoroethylene Carbonate on Lithium Metal Anodes via a Solvent-Free
Model System
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) is a widely used film-forming additive for stabilizing lithium metal anodes (LMAs), yet its intrinsic interfacial chemistry remains elusive because its reactions are coupled with those of solvents and Li salts in conventional electrolytes. Herein, a solvent-free, dry-processed poly(ethylene oxide)-based solid polymer electrolyte (PEO@Dry) is developed as a platform to isolate the interfacial reactions of FEC without interference from traditional liquid organic solvents. PEO@Dry retains the intrinsic interfacial reactivity of PEO and LiTFSI while eliminating solvent-derived interference. FEC is found to undergo a spontaneous chemical reaction with Li metal before electrochemical reduction, producing a dense LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that is subsequently reinforced by organic species derived from the electrochemical reactions. The resulting SEI exhibits a well-defined composition and robust structure, leading to an enhanced interfacial stability and electrochemical performance. Comparative research with a DME-based liquid electrolyte reveals that FEC (DME@FEC) follows distinct reaction pathways depending on its solvation state. In the solvent-free PEO@Dry system, free FEC undergoes sequential chemical and electrochemical reduction to form an inorganic-rich SEI, whereas in the liquid electrolyte, FEC participates in Li+ solvation and competes with other electrolyte components, yielding a more complex SEI. This work clarifies the interfacial mechanism of FEC and establishes a general solvent-free platform for mechanistic studies of electrolyte additives on LMAs.

papers.title: Local Characterization of Global Tensor Network Eigenstates
papers.titleOriginal: Local Characterization of Global Tensor Network Eigenstates
papers.journal: Physical Review Letters
papers.subject: Physics
papers.abstract: We study the conditions under which Matrix Product States (MPS) or Matrix Product Operators are exact eigenvectors of an extensive local operator, such as a Hamiltonian. By suitably choosing the local operator, this covers a wide range of settings: Exact eigenstates of Hamiltonians, including scar states, exact MPS trajectories for driven quantum systems, steady states of local Lindbladians, generalized symmetries of either Hamiltonians or density matrices, and many more. Our key result is that a local, fixed-size equation---namely, how a single term in the operator acts on a block of tensors---provides a necessary and sufficient condition for exact solutions. This local characterization allows us to obtain the full space of MPS solutions to all of the aforementioned problems; in particular, we exemplify the power of our results by recovering the quantum group symmetries of the XXZ model. We also discuss applications to numerical algorithms with MPS and the generalization of our results to 2D, i.e., projected entangled pair states (PEPS).

papers.titleOriginal: Molecular mapping of an exoplanet with JWST: Detection of NH3 and HCN in the temperate super-Jupiter Epsilon Indi Ab
papers.journal: Astronomy & Astrophysics
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Epsilon Indi Ab is currently the coldest and one of the closest directly imaged exoplanets (T_ eff = 275 K, d=3.6 pc). It offers a unique opportunity to test our understanding of the physical and chemical properties of gas giants across the full temperature range spanned by hotter directly imaged exoplanets and the cooler giants of the Solar System. We characterize the atmosphere of Epsilon Indi Ab using infrared spectroscopic observations. We present JWST spectroscopic observations of Epsilon Indi Ab obtained with MIRI in the medium-resolution spectrograph mode (4.9--27.9 μm) and NIRSpec in the integral field unit mode (2.87--5.27 μm). The data are highly contaminated by the stellar light from the bright host star. We therefore adopted a high-pass filtering and cross-correlation approach based on atmospheric models to detect the planetary signal and specific molecules. petitRADTRANS The cross-correlation analysis enabled us to robustly detect the planet with both instruments with a signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) up to mathrm S/N =15.0. Using molecular mapping, we securely identified the presence of (maximum mathrm NH3 S/N = 14.4), (maximum mathrm H2O S/N = 11.3), (mathrm HCN S/N = 5.3) and marginally detected (mathrm PH3 S/N = 4.1), (mathrm CH4 S/N = 3.8), (mathrm C2H2 S/N = 3.9) and (mathrm CO2 S/N = 2.6). In particular, Epsilon Indi Ab becomes the coldest exoplanet in which and have been identified so far. The presence of HCN likely implies intense vertical mixing. NH3 HCN These first results confirm that infrared spectroscopy combined with cross-correlation techniques can be used to characterize the atmosphere of directly imaged exoplanets with JWST, even when the contamination by the host star is critical.

papers.title: (203) Pompeja: Constraining a non-convex shape model, size, and bulk density to support the interpretation of its spectral variability
papers.titleOriginal: (203) Pompeja: Constraining a non-convex shape model, size, and bulk density to support the interpretation of its spectral variability
papers.journal: Astronomy & Astrophysics
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Recent stellar occultations of (203) Pompeja provided well-constrained silhouettes that had the potential to enable a more detailed reconstruction of its three-dimensional shape. Motivated by these data, we aimed to reconstruct the asteroid spin and shape model using the ADAM (All-Data Asteroid Modeling) method and to use the improved model to test the hypothesis that the reported spectral-slope variability is related to specific surface regions. We also aimed to resolve the mirror-pole ambiguity and improve the determination of Pompeja size and bulk density. We applied the ADAM method to a combined dataset consisting of photometric light curves and six stellar occultation events. It allowed us to constrain Pompeja's non-convex three-dimensional shape, sidereal rotation period, and spin axis orientation. The determined volume-equivalent diameter was subsequently combined with an available mass estimate to determine the bulk density. To investigate the possible spectral variability, we reconstructed illumination and viewing geometries of the ADAM spin and shape model for the available spectroscopic observations and quantitatively compared the surface regions sampled at different epochs. We also performed a facet-based correlation analysis between the shape model and measured spectral slopes. Finally, we modelled the spectral slopes by jointly accounting for surface-dependent and observing geometry effects and used this model to predict favourable geometries for future observations. We obtained a unique spin and shape solution for Pompeja and resolved the pole ambiguity. Preferred spin axis orientation is found to be łambda = 132 ^ +6 _ -1 deg and β = 39 ^ +8 _ -1 deg. papers.title: Detection of TeV emission during early afterglow from poorly localized gamma-ray bursts with ground-based IACTs
papers.titleOriginal: Detection of TeV emission during early afterglow from poorly localized gamma-ray bursts with ground-based IACTs
papers.journal: Astronomy & Astrophysics
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are among the most luminous and rapidly evolving transients in the Universe. While space-based instruments have extended GRB observations up to energies of ∼100 GeV, the detection of very high-energy (VHE; E>100 GeV) emission from ground-based telescopes, especially during prompt and/or the early afterglow phases, remains challenging. These difficulties arise from the rapid temporal decay of GRB afterglows, strong attenuation by the extragalactic background light, observational latency, and the typical poor sky localization provided by MeV detectors such as Fermi/GBM. In this work, we investigated the prospects for detecting TeV (∼100 GeV--1 TeV) emission from poorly localized GRBs by adopting optimized follow-up strategies based on rapid tiling of large localization regions. We simulated a realistic population of GRBs informed by more than 15 years of Fermi/GBM and Swift/XRT detections and recent progress in the afterglow emission modeling. Using these simulations, we evaluated the detectability of GRB early afterglows by the next-generation imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, which are equipped with larger fields of view, as a function of latency, exposure time, and observational strategy. Our strategy can significantly enhance the detection rate; for instruments such as ASTRI and LACT, it increases by up to a factor of two compared to strategies limited to well-localized (Swift-like) events. For CTAO, our proposed approach provides up to four VHE detections per year.

Differential dust attenuation dims galaxy centers and creates larger sizes, modifying the mass-size slope even in the rest-frame optical. At a fixed mass, the galaxy size evolves very fast because the normalization of the size-mass relation increases by 0.5 dex between z and z within 600 Myr. The SFR surface density increases with redshift, driven by higher sSFRs and smaller sizes at higher redshifts. The size evolution at a fixed stellar mass accelerates at cosmic dawn, driven by an increasing galaxy efficiency at z

papers.title: Machine learning technique for morphological classification of galaxies from SDSS. IV. CNN-assisted expert validation of morphological catalogues for merging, irregular, edge-on, barred, ringed, and dust-lane galaxies at 0.003 < z < 0.1
papers.titleOriginal: Machine learning technique for morphological classification of galaxies from SDSS. IV. CNN-assisted expert validation of morphological catalogues for merging, irregular, edge-on, barred, ringed, and dust-lane galaxies at 0.003 < z < 0.1
papers.journal: Astronomy & Astrophysics
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have become an efficient tool for automated classification of galaxy morphology in large astronomical surveys. However, identifying complex morphological features remains limited by projection effects, image artefacts, and intrinsic ambiguities, making expert visual validation essential to building reliable morphological catalogues. This paper introduces a CNN-assisted expert validation framework for constructing reliable galaxy image-based morphological catalogues. Our goal was to use this framework to perform a comprehensive visual validation of Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) galaxies at 0.003<z<0.1 previously classified by a CNN as merging, irregular, edge-on, barred, ringed, or dust-lane galaxies; to quantify the reliability and failure modes of CNN classifications; to construct homogeneous and visually verified catalogues of these morphological classes; and to characterise the central ionisation of the verified galaxies with emission-line diagnostics. We visually inspected all CNN-selected candidates in four morphological categories, namely merging (2,574), irregular (9,432), ringed (13,882), and dust-lane (588) galaxies, covering the full range of their catalogue feature scores. For edge-on and barred galaxies, we inspected the 17,000 and 4,323 highest-scoring candidates, respectively, which we selected from larger CNN catalogues. We cross-matched the refined samples with the Galaxy Zoo 2 (GZ2) catalogue, and we visually classified galaxies outside its selection domain, which carry no GZ2 morphological label. For the subset with SDSS spectroscopy, we applied the Baldwin--Phillips--Terlevich (BPT) and the N, ii /Hα versus Hα equivalent width (WHAN) diagnostics to the MPA--JHU emission-line measurements. We present homogeneous, visually verified catalogues containing 612 merging galaxies, 9,372 irregular galaxies, 16,822 edge-on galaxies, 811 barred galaxies, 2,145 ringed galaxies, and 575 dust-lane galaxies. Comparison with GZ2 demonstrates that CNN-assisted expert validation both refines existing classifications and extends reliable morphological catalogues beyond the effective Galaxy Zoo selection domain. The principal causes of CNN misclassification are projection effects, foreground stars, image artefacts, faint tidal structures, and intrinsically ambiguous morphologies. Emission-line diagnostics show that 87.8% of the ringed galaxies with low-ionisation nuclear emission-line region (LINER)-like line ratios have Hα equivalent widths consistent with ionisation by evolved stars rather than by an active nucleus. We also identified five strong new candidates for polar ring galaxies. Our results demonstrate that CNN-assisted expert validation remains essential for constructing reliable galaxy morphological catalogues. The resulting homogeneous datasets provide valuable resources for studies of galaxy morphology, secular evolution, and nuclear activity, and they constitute high-quality benchmark samples for future machine learning applications and forthcoming wide-field surveys.

papers.abstract: Abstract Deuterium labeling plays a pivotal role in pharmaceutical development by modulating physicochemical properties and enabling metabolic tracing. papers.abstract: Abstract Owing to their promising bioactivities, unusually high nitrogen and halogen contents, and distinctive polycyclic architectures, the family of pyrrole-imidazole alkaloids continues to attract significant attention. papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Ion-Association Design Decouples Linearity and Dynamic Range in Organic Electrochemical Synapses
papers.titleOriginal:
Artificial Intelligence-Assisted
Ion-Association Design
Decouples Linearity and Dynamic Range in Organic Electrochemical Synapses
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Organic electrochemical synaptic transistors (OESTs) are promising neuromorphic devices, but simultaneously achieving highly linear analog weight updates and a wide dynamic range remains fundamentally limited by a severe trade-off in uncontrolled interface doping kinetics. Although multicomponent electrolytes offer a pathway to tune ion behavior, a predictive framework capable of overcoming this strict trade-off remains unexplored due to the highly nonlinear nature of interionic interactions. Here, we introduce an AI-assisted ion-association design strategy utilizing a binary electrolyte architecture to break through the linearity–dynamic range trade-off. GPR-assisted regression analysis maps complex electrolyte formulations to synaptic nonlinearity, identifying an optimized NaCl·Na-TFSI binary configuration. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggest distinct intrinsic ion-association tendencies between Na+–Cl– and Na+–TFSI– pairs, consistent with the observed doping and relaxation behaviors: strongly associated Na+–Cl– pairs suppress abrupt doping to optimize linearity, reducing nonlinearity by up to ∼6-fold compared with single-anion controls, while weakly associated Na+–TFSI– pairs facilitate ion retention to expand the dynamic range (Gmax/Gmin ∼ 103). This balanced dual-anion transport enables linear, extensible, and high-dynamic-range multistate conductance modulation. Consequently, the optimized OESTs exhibit improved LTP/D linearity, reproducible cycling, and a 94.88% MNIST recognition accuracy. These results establish predictive binary ion-association design as a general framework for controlling synaptic weight modulation in organic neuromorphic devices.

papers.abstract: Order-disorder transitions allow many proteins to shift between compact and flexible/unfolded states, thereby acting as structural switches that regulate catalysis, signaling, recognition, and allostery. Our per-residue density analysis provides a detailed structural-kinetic basis for understanding how order-disorder transitions emerge through directional propagation across protein tertiary structures, as occurring in signaling and many other biological systems.

papers.titleOriginal:
Control of Charge Carrier
Dynamics and Bandgap Renormalization

papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Charge carrier dynamics in wurtzite CdS quantum dots (QDs) form the basis for applications in optoelectronics and photocatalysis. We demonstrate that the quantum dynamics, energy gaps, and energy level alignments at CdS QD interfaces can be controlled by the polarity of the CdS QD surface. By performing nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations within a density-functional tight-binding framework, we demonstrate a strong dependence of photoinitiated processes in CdS QDs/graphene nanoribbon (GNR) hybrids on interface polarity. At room temperature, hole transfer is accelerated by a factor of 2 and exciton lifetime is enhanced by nearly an order of magnitude when the CdS QD surface is switched from polar to nonpolar. Remarkably, the interfacial bandgap for the polar QD/GNR hybrid is reduced to half upon heating from 0 K to room temperature, while it remains nearly unchanged for the nonpolar hybrid. At an intermediate temperature, the ultrafast charge separation is maintained; however, charge recombination shows the opposite trend relative to room temperature. The polar interface exhibits a longer lifetime than the nonpolar interface, due to weakened electron–phonon Fröhlich interaction and decreased gap renormalization. The strong and highly nonlinear dependence of bandgap renormalization and carrier dynamics on temperature in the polar QD/GNR hybrid is associated with significant structural reconstruction, which is absent in the nonpolar counterpart. The demonstrated control of excited-state processes by interface polarity and the strong dependence of the dynamics and energy level alignment on temperature provide key fundamental insights for informed design of modern materials for optoelectronics and energy conversion.

papers.abstract: Abstract Biomarker-specific molecular imaging is vital in precision medicine. However, a fundamental challenge of most molecular imaging methods is the difficulty of distinguishing specific molecular signal from nonspecific signal arising from the distribution of the molecular probe. This is even more pronounced in metabolically active organs such as the kidney and liver where the probe may concentrate prior to elimination. As a result, almost all molecular imaging relies on delayed imaging to achieve specificity, but this constrains clinical throughput and impedes rapid assessment of the diseased organ. Here, we report a magnetic resonance (MR) probe, Fe(II)-IAFP2, which combines 3 drivers of relaxivity enhancement to decouple disease specificity from probe distribution. Fe(II)-IAFP2 is MR-silent in its Fe(II) state, producing negligible MR signal even at high concentrations. In inflammatory, fibrogenic microenvironments common to many diseases, rapid oxidation to Fe(III) activates MR enhancement, while reversible aldehyde-mediated binding to remodeled extracellular matrix further amplifies relaxivity and promotes retention at the site of tissue injury. This dual activation–retention mechanism enables robust signal generation within minutes of administration. In mouse models of renal and liver fibrogenesis, Fe(II)-IAFP2 generated disease-associated MR contrast within minutes after intravenous administration. Together, this work demonstrates an effective strategy for rapid, activity-based molecular MR imaging through the combination of pathological activation and complementary tissue retention.

papers.title: Anti -Dihydroxylation-Enabled Dual-Resolution Profiling and Imaging of Fatty Acid C═C Bond Isomers
papers.titleOriginal: Anti -Dihydroxylation-Enabled Dual-Resolution Profiling and Imaging of Fatty Acid C═C Bond Isomers
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Lipids are essential for membrane structure, signaling, and stress adaptation. Their diverse biological roles are largely dictated by the presence of C═C bonds in unsaturated fatty acids (FAs), which vary in both position and geometry. However, unambiguous characterization and in situ mapping of these two structural features have remained longstanding analytical challenges. Here, we present a stereochemistry-preserved chemical derivatization strategy coupled with trapped ion mobility spectrometry-tandem MS (TIMS-MS/MS), enabling complete resolution of both FA C═C bond position and geometry within a single workflow. This approach facilitates rapid and quantitative profiling of dynamic cis–trans isomerization in bacteria under diverse stress conditions and, notably, reveals a previously unrecognized dose-dependent antibiotic adaptation mechanism in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a multidrug-resistant pathogen. To translate this strategy to spatially resolved analyses, we developed an in situ derivatization workflow for mass spectrometry imaging, which uncovers the spatial heterogeneity of FA isomers in proximally cocultured, clinically relevant polymicrobial pathogens. These findings highlight colony-specific spatial dynamics of cis and trans lipid isomers and suggest lipid-mediated metabolic interactions between co-occurring microbial species. Together, this integrated platform enables both quantitative and spatial interrogation of lipid isomerization, providing new opportunities to systematically investigate its roles in microbial physiology, pathogenesis, and beyond.

papers.title: Orbital decomposition and evolution of LEGA-C -like galaxies in IllustrisTNG from z=1 to z=0
papers.titleOriginal: Orbital decomposition and evolution of LEGA-C -like galaxies in IllustrisTNG from z=1 to z=0
papers.journal: Astronomy & Astrophysics
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Stellar orbits encode the dynamical history of galaxies and provide a physically motivated link between galaxy structures and assembly processes. Although orbit-based decompositions are well established in the Local Universe, their evolution across cosmic time, especially at higher redshifts, remains poorly explored. We investigate the orbital structure of galaxies in the simulation from z=1 to z=0 to identify how stellar mass, star formation activity, environment, merger history, gas content, and ex situ stellar mass growth shape their orbital transformation. LEGA-C-like TNG100 We decomposed the stellar orbital structure of simulated galaxies into cold, warm, hot, and counter-rotating (CR) components using time-averaged orbital circularities. This provides a theoretical basis for future comparisons with Schwarzschild-based orbital decompositions of observed galaxies. We analyzed the galaxy populations at z=1 and z=0, then tracked the descendants of individual z=1 galaxies to quantify their orbital evolution over this time. We find a strong mass dependence of orbital structure at z=0 as well as at z=1. Galaxies below łog(M_⋆/M_⊙) have a combined warm and cold orbital fraction of sim70%, whereas more massive systems have a hot-orbit fraction of sim60%. These trends are consistent with assembly pathways driven predominantly by wet and dry major mergers, respectively. Tracking the same galaxies to z=0 reveals a systematic, but mass-dependent, evolution toward lower rotational support: At both low and high stellar masses, the hot-orbit fraction increases, whereas the relative change is greater in low-mass galaxies. The survival of cold structure depends strongly on the star formation state at z=1; star-forming progenitors retain substantially larger cold fractions than the quiescent progenitors. At both redshifts, the orbital fractions show a rise (decline) in hot and CR (cold and warm) orbits with the ex situ stellar mass fraction at a fixed stellar mass. These results provide the first evolutionary framework for interpreting orbit-based decompositions of galaxies at the epoch. Stellar orbital fractions quantify the morphological and dynamical transformation of galaxies and show systematic evolutionary trends at the population level. Individual galaxies, however, follow diverse evolutionary pathways. Comparisons to future Schwarzschild-based decompositions of observed high-redshift galaxies can use these results to interpret the internal physical structure of galaxy populations and constrain theoretical models of galaxy evolution. papers.title: Mechanism-Guided Development of Thioacetylene Probes for Chemoproteomic Profiling of Cellular Protein Thiyl Radicals
papers.titleOriginal:
Mechanism-Guided Development
of Thioacetylene Probes
for Chemoproteomic Profiling of Cellular Protein Thiyl Radicals
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Protein thiyl radicals are transient reactive intermediates involved in oxidative stress and enzymatic catalysis. However, their proteome-wide, site-resolved profiling in living cells remains challenging due to the lack of suitable tools. Here, we report chemoproteomic probes enabling covalent capture and site-resolved identification of protein thiyl radicals in living cells. Designed to leverage sulfur-mediated stabilization of a vinyl radical intermediate, our thioacetylene-based probes selectively capture cysteine thiyl radicals while minimizing cross-reactivity with nucleophilic thiolates and nonradical amino acid residues. In vitro validation and live-cell chemoproteomic analysis established radical-dependent labeling and site-resolved detection of protein thiyl radicals. Notably, the probes enabled site-specific mapping of thiyl radical-associated cysteine residues in live E. coli, including Cys439 of ribonucleotide reductase A (NrdA), a canonical enzymatic thiyl radical site. Expanded residue profiling further confirmed cysteine-predominant labeling and detected probe modification at established and putative glycyl radical residues in PflB, NrdD, and YjjI, suggesting that the platform may extend beyond thiyl radicals to other protein-centered radicals. Application of the probe under oxidative and nitrosative stress revealed condition-dependent changes in cellular protein radical-associated labeling, including decreased labeling at established glycyl radical residues and bidirectional changes in cysteine radical-associated labeling. Together, these findings establish thioacetylene probes as a platform for site-resolved mapping and comparative monitoring of endogenous protein-centered radicals in living cells.

papers.title: Synergistic Interactions Enable Superior Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity in Compositionally Complex Nanocrystal–Nanosheet Hybrids
papers.titleOriginal:
Synergistic Interactions
Enable Superior Oxygen Evolution
Reaction Activity in Compositionally Complex Nanocrystal–Nanosheet
Hybrids
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Thiospinel nanoparticles are promising catalytic materials due to their compositional tunability, electronic conductivity, and structural stability. While significant gains in catalysis have been made through material engineering, one continuously developing route is through the use of support materials to enhance performance. Here, we report a simple, scalable, low-temperature method to coproduce colloidal multimetal nanocrystals (<20 nm in diameter) and In2S3-based nanosheets (<1 nm thick), forming compositionally complex hybrid nanocrystal–nanosheet heterostructures in situ. The in situ-formed heterostructures demonstrate enhanced catalytic activity in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in alkaline conditions; peak performance was achieved in heterostructures formed between (Ni,Co,Fe)3S4 nanocrystals and (In,Fe,Mn)2S3 nanosheets with overpotentials as low as 283 mV at 10 mA/cm2. Heterostructures can also be produced ex situ by introducing nanosheets, postsynthetically, to the nanocrystals, reducing the overpotential of (Ni,Co,Fe)3S4 nanocrystals from 362 mV to 312 mV with only a 5 wt % addition. This improvement highlights synergistic interactions in the heterostructures. These results suggest that an optimum nanosheet loading that maximizes effective nanocrystal–nanosheet interfacial coupling while preserving access to the Ni/Co-rich catalytic domains is the relevant design parameter. Our findings provide a low-temperature, colloidal route for synthesizing compositionally complex and highly uniform (<15% dispersity) sulfide nanocrystals, nanosheets, or heterostructures of the two with tunable structures and enhanced electrocatalytic performance. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a compositionally complex hybrid material that is able to enhance performance when formed both in situ or ex situ and the use of In2S3 as a scaffold for a support material for enhancing OER performance.

papers.title: Enantioselective Three-Component Reductive Coupling of Aldehydes, Amines, and Alkynes via Ligand-Enabled Cobalt/Photoredox Dual Catalysis for Modular Synthesis of Allylic Amines
papers.titleOriginal:
Enantioselective Three-Component
Reductive Coupling
of Aldehydes, Amines, and Alkynes via Ligand-Enabled Cobalt/Photoredox
Dual Catalysis for Modular Synthesis of Allylic Amines
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Here, we disclose a catalytic strategy that merges visible-light photoredox with cobalt catalysis to realize a previously elusive three-component enantioselective reductive coupling of readily available aldehydes, amines, and alkynes. This transformation provides a direct, step-economical route to high-value chiral allylic amines with broad substrate scope and high chemo-, regio-, and enantioselectivity, while overcoming long-standing challenges, including parasitic single-electron over-reduction, competitive aldehyde–alkyne coupling, and the inherent regioselectivity issues of unsymmetrical internal alkynes, and circumventing the moisture sensitivity and limited scope of pre-isolated imines. Central to this breakthrough is the rational design of a chiral phosphoramidite ligand featuring a tricyclic tetrahydrobenzoquinoline core, which avoids coordination saturation at cobalt and establishes a unique electronic “push–pull” synergy with a coordinated iodide anion. Mechanistic studies support an anion-promoted, single-ligand catalytic model wherein a high-spin cobaltacyclopentene intermediate serves as the key stereocontrol element. The monodentate, π-accepting phosphoramidite functions as a flexible electronic buffer, mitigating Pauli repulsion and dramatically lowering the oxidative cyclization barrier. The synthetic utility is demonstrated by late-stage functionalization of complex bioactive molecules and a concise synthesis of the antiplatelet drug prasugrel.
